title: POC Tactician: weekly retro and task grid
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a customer-facing POC engagement (6-week cadence) focused on getting a narrow LLM feature into production. The doc is intentionally pragmatic: a compact arc from discovery -> hands-on workshop -> integration spike -> validation -> scale test -> handoff. Use this as the main running artifact during the engagement; keep the Decision Log updated each week.

Outcome Hypothesis:
- Primary business outcome: Customer reduces time-to-resolution on support tickets by 40% using a Redwood-hosted scoring/generation endpoint.
- Technical outcome: Stable inference at 95th percentile latency <= 220ms for 256-token responses in dedicated test harness.

Success metrics (agreed with customer):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 220ms under target QPS (10qps sustained, 30qps burst).
- Cost: Token unit cost target <= $0.0025 (hosted equivalence) for production-like traffic profile.
- Quality: F1 >= 0.78 on canonical evaluation set (50 curated prompts).
- Ops: No more than 2 incidents during the 2-week scale test.

Primary stakeholders:
- Customer PM: Leah Hernandez
- Customer Tech Lead: Omar Basri
- Redwood SE lead: Evelyn Park (owner)
- Redwood Ops: Marcus Liu
- Success/Engagement sponsor: Priya Ramesh

High-level 6-week plan (compressed timeline):
- Week 0 (Prep) - Pre-engagement checklist, account setup, data access, privacy guard-rails
  - Deliverables: access tokens, data sample, baseline eval run (seed prompts)
  - Acceptance: baseline eval uploaded to shared test folder and passes smoke run

- Week 1 (Workshop) - 2-day remote workshop + 1 day integration prep
  - Day 1: Customer context, user journeys, show-and-tell of Redwood runtime, streaming demo
  - Day 2: Mapping prompts -> routes, determine model variants, sketch rollback policy
  - Deliverable: Workshop artifact (intent-to-solution sketch), route config draft
  - Acceptance: Customer sign-off on route config and SLA targets for the POC

- Week 2 (Integration spike) - on-customer-infra test harness; deploy test model variant
  - Tasks: API keys, small dedicated pool config, KV caching opt-in, example SDK integration (node/python)
  - Deliverable: End-to-end smoke integration (customer app -> Redwood test endpoint)
  - Acceptance: Smoke test passes in staging with no auth/networking blockers

- Week 3 (Eval & tuning) - run curated evals, iterate prompt templates, quantization recommendations
  - Tasks: schedule eval run, collect mismatch samples, iterate prompt scaffolding
  - Deliverable: Evaluation report + recommended quantization and batching profile
  - Acceptance: Quality and latency tradeoffs documented; customer agrees to one tuning path

- Week 4 (Scale test) - synthetic load representing production; observe autoscaling and failovers
  - Tasks: load plan, latency SLO checks, fallback drills (lower-capacity variant), tracing enabled
  - Deliverable: Scale-test runbook and incident playbacks
  - Acceptance: Meets latency/cost targets OR documented constraints + rollback plan

- Week 5 (Handoff & retro) - run final handoff, knowledge transfer, billing/contract next steps
  - Tasks: finalize infra recommendations (Dedicated vs Private), operational runbook, retention plan
  - Deliverable: Handoff doc, action items for post-POC committed work
  - Acceptance: Customer greenlights pilot or requests specific follow-ups

Compact task grid (use as the canonical living list each week). Columns: ID | Task | Owner | Est (hrs) | Dep | Status | Acceptance criteria
- T1 | Collect sample dataset & seed prompts | Omar Basri | 16h | - | in_progress | Sample contains 200 seed prompts + labels
- T2 | Baseline eval in Redwood console | Marcus Liu | 6h | T1 | done | Baseline report uploaded to shared drive
- T3 | Workshop slides + hands-on workbook | Evelyn Park | 12h | - | done | Slides in drive, workshop workbook tested locally
- T4 | Staging API key + integration guide | Dylan Ortiz | 10h | T2 | in_progress | SDK examples run end-to-end in staging
- T5 | Config dedicated test pool & autoscale policy | Marcus Liu | 8h | T4 | todo | Pool spins up and accepts traffic from test harness
- T6 | Eval harness run & tuning pass | Sofia Nguyen | 14h | T5 | todo | Evaluation artifact with latency and quality tables
- T7 | Scale test (load generator) | Evelyn Park | 18h | T5,T6 | todo | 10qps sustained run completes, SLO dashboard populated
- T8 | Incident tabletop + rollback drill | Marcus Liu | 6h | T7 | todo | Drill executed with <15min mean recovery time
- T9 | Handoff doc + ops playbook | Priya Ramesh | 8h | T7,T8 | todo | Ops playbook signed off by customer engineers

Decision log (short):
- D1 (2024-10-03): Picked model family: open Llama-derived 13B as baseline. Rationale: customer data residency and cost. (owner: Evelyn)
- D2 (2024-10-10): Enable KV-prefix caching for repeated conversation threads in test pool. (owner: Marcus)
- D3 (2024-10-18): Use dedicated test pool rather than hosted ephemeral endpoints for consistent latency profiling. (owner: Evelyn)

Open questions / risks:
- Data availability: customer may not provide canonical evaluation labels in time (mitigation: use heuristics labeling + active sampling).
- Network egress limits: customer's VPC firewall rules may throttle test harness (mitigation: schedule firewall window and use temporary CIDR allowlist).
- Latency variance under cold-starts: quantify via multiple cold-start cycles and add warmup startup step in runbook.

Workshop agenda (Day 1 condensed):
- 09:00 - 09:15 Introductions + success metrics align
- 09:15 - 10:00 Customer product walkthrough (user journeys)
- 10:00 - 11:00 Redwood runtime deep-dive (serving runtime, routing, caching)
- 11:00 - 12:30 Hands-on SDK demo + sample integration
- 13:30 - 15:30 Breakouts: prompts -> routes mapping (small groups)
- 15:30 - 16:15 Draft route config + fallback policy discussion
- 16:15 - 16:45 Next steps + immediate action items

Retro snapshot (post-week-1):
- What went well: Customer engaged early, APIs accessible, workshop produced clear route candidate
- What to change: Need earlier data-format templates from customer; workshop workbook could have clearer error troubleshooting tips for SDKs
- Actions: Add a one-page sample-CSV schema, add network troubleshooting appendix to workbook (action: Dylan, 3d)

Operational runbook highlights (to append to final):
- Recommended fixed params for test pool: batch_size=8, max_tokens=512, kv_cache=true
- Quantization: recommend int8-quant variant for cost/latency tradeoff; keep float16 for high-quality baseline
- Autoscale policy suggestion: target CPU/GPU utilization 60-70% with burst to 100% for 5m windows; enable graceful queueing beyond SLO threshold
- Rollback: immediate fallback to smaller model family + degrade to streaming-only responses if latency spikes >300ms for 5min

Communication matrix during POC (who to ping):
- Incidents: Marcus (SRE) -> Slack #cust-poc-incidents / PagerDuty
- Product clarifications: Evelyn -> Slack thread + weekly review
- Billing/next-steps: Priya -> GTM contact and Salesforce opportunity update

Appendix: quick checklist before scale test
- Confirm canonical eval set uploaded (Owner: Omar)
- Verify autoscaler policy final (Owner: Marcus)
- Enable tracing at debug level for 24h prior to run (Owner: Dylan)
- Ensure KMS keys provisioned for any private deployment artifacts (Owner: Priya)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep workshop workbook intentionally terse; customers hate 40-slide decks in hands-on sessions.
- If customer expresses strong security needs, accelerate private deployment assessment (need SSO/KMS checklist).
- Follow up on SE-4123 — it contains a useful tracing snippet that saved ~35ms per token in a prior POC (link above).

Next immediate actions (first 72h):
- Evelyn: finalize workshop workbook + prep breakout prompts (12h)
- Marcus: provision test pool and share staging key (6h)
- Omar: drop sample dataset into shared drive and confirm labels (8h)
- Dylan: validate SDK examples connect to staging (6h)

End of working draft. Update Decision Log and Task Grid weekly.
